references.text: Mentions the Jebusites and Jerusalem, showing that the Jebusites lived in Jerusalem before the Israelites took over the city.
Describes how the Jebusites continued to live in Jerusalem alongside the people of Judah, indicating the city's divided status among the tribes.
The introduction to Benjamin's inheritance, showing that Jerusalem lay on the border between Judah and Benjamin.
States that the people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem, and they continued to live there.
Gibeah in Benjamin is mentioned as Saul's hometown, one of the cities belonging to the tribe of Benjamin.
David conquers Jerusalem from the Jebusites, a city previously noted as part of Benjamin's inheritance.
The first time the Jebusites are mentioned in the Bible as one of the peoples of Canaan.
